   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# alluvial tutorial: how modules change\n",
    "\n",
    "This tutorial draws alluvial diagrams of [Infomap](https://www.mapequation.org/infomap/) partitions with\n",
    "`alluvial`. It covers how to:\n",
    "\n",
    "1. compare the partitions of several Infomap runs,\n",
    "2. choose a coloring,\n",
    "3. show sub-modules,\n",
    "4. highlight groups of nodes, with a legend,\n",
    "5. draw state networks (multilayer and memory networks),\n",
    "6. read Infomap output files,\n",
    "7. make a multi-panel figure for a paper and save it as PDF, and\n",
    "8. restyle single artists.\n",
    "\n",
    "You need `pip install \"alluvial[infomap]\"`. Every network is built in the notebook and every Infomap run is\n",
    "seeded, so the figures come out the same each time."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "39138d8c",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-21T09:16:37.427866Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-21T09:16:37.424962Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-21T09:16:39.019973Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-21T09:16:38.996330Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import random\n",
    "\n",
    "import infomap\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "\n",
    "import alluvial"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "a2d9aa30",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## A small temporal network\n",
    "\n",
    "Here 36 people work in teams of six, and teams that share a department collaborate. Over three years the\n",
    "departments reorganize. In 2022 one team moves to another department, and in 2023 three departments become two.\n",
    "For each year, links are drawn at random: dense within teams, sparser within departments, and rare between them."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "07a6d916",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-21T09:16:39.028908Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-21T09:16:39.027646Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-21T09:16:39.526880Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-21T09:16:39.525179Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "2021: 4 top modules, 3 levels, codelength 3.614 bits\n",
      "2022: 4 top modules, 3 levels, codelength 3.787 bits\n",
      "2023: 4 top modules, 3 levels, codelength 4.093 bits\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "NAMES = [\n",
    "    \"Ada\",\n",
    "    \"Ben\",\n",
    "    \"Cy\",\n",
    "    \"Dee\",\n",
    "    \"Eli\",\n",
    "    \"Fay\",\n",
    "    \"Gus\",\n",
    "    \"Hal\",\n",
    "    \"Ivy\",\n",
    "    \"Jo\",\n",
    "    \"Kai\",\n",
    "    \"Lea\",\n",
    "    \"Max\",\n",
    "    \"Ned\",\n",
    "    \"Ola\",\n",
    "    \"Pia\",\n",
    "    \"Quin\",\n",
    "    \"Rex\",\n",
    "    \"Sam\",\n",
    "    \"Tia\",\n",
    "    \"Uma\",\n",
    "    \"Vic\",\n",
    "    \"Wes\",\n",
    "    \"Xia\",\n",
    "    \"Yan\",\n",
    "    \"Zoe\",\n",
    "    \"Abe\",\n",
    "    \"Bea\",\n",
    "    \"Cal\",\n",
    "    \"Dot\",\n",
    "    \"Eve\",\n",
    "    \"Fin\",\n",
    "    \"Gil\",\n",
    "    \"Hana\",\n",
    "    \"Ike\",\n",
    "    \"Jan\",\n",
    "]\n",
    "TEAMS = [range(k, k + 6) for k in range(0, 36, 6)]  # six teams of six people\n",
    "YEARS = [\"2021\", \"2022\", \"2023\"]\n",
    "DEPARTMENTS = {  # the teams of each department, per year\n",
    "    \"2021\": [[0, 1], [2, 3], [4, 5]],\n",
    "    \"2022\": [[0, 1], [2, 3, 4], [5]],\n",
    "    \"2023\": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]],\n",
    "}\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "def collaborations(departments, seed):\n",
    "    \"Random links: dense within teams, sparser within departments, rare between departments.\"\n",
    "    rng = random.Random(seed)\n",
    "    team = {u: t for t, members in enumerate(TEAMS) for u in members}\n",
    "    dept = {t: d for d, teams in enumerate(departments) for t in teams}\n",
    "    links = []\n",
    "    for u in range(36):\n",
    "        for v in range(u + 1, 36):\n",
    "            if team[u] == team[v]:\n",
    "                p = 0.7\n",
    "            elif dept[team[u]] == dept[team[v]]:\n",
    "                p = 0.12\n",
    "            else:\n",
    "                p = 0.01\n",
    "            if rng.random() < p:\n",
    "                links.append((u, v))\n",
    "    return links\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "links = {year: collaborations(DEPARTMENTS[year], seed=i) for i, year in enumerate(YEARS)}\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "def run_infomap(links):\n",
    "    im = infomap.Infomap(seed=42, num_trials=10, silent=True)\n",
    "    for u, name in enumerate(NAMES):\n",
    "        im.add_node(u, name)\n",
    "    im.add_links(links)\n",
    "    im.run()\n",
    "    return im\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "im_a, im_b, im_c = (run_infomap(links[year]) for year in YEARS)\n",
    "for year, im in zip(YEARS, (im_a, im_b, im_c)):\n",
    "    nf = alluvial.read(im)  # the partition as alluvial reads it\n",
    "    paths = [node.path.split(\":\") for node in nf.nodes]  # \"1:2:3\": module 1, sub-module 2, node 3\n",
    "    top_modules = {path[0] for path in paths}\n",
    "    levels = max(map(len, paths))\n",
    "    print(f\"{year}: {len(top_modules)} top modules, {levels} levels, codelength {nf.codelength:.3f} bits\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "d2e25bd9",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## One diagram for several runs\n",
    "\n",
    "Pass the Infomap objects from left to right. Each column is a network, and each block a module, with its height\n",
    "proportional to the module's flow. A streamline joins two modules and is as thick as the flow of the nodes they\n",
    "share. Nodes are matched across networks by node id. Modules carry the names of their largest nodes (by flow) on the\n",
    "first and last network."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,

   ]

   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Colors\n",
    "\n",
    "`colors=` picks how modules are colored. Every option is an operation of the web app:\n",
    "\n",
    "- `\"module_id\"` (the default) gives each module id one color, the same in every network,\n",
    "- `\"similarity\"` gives matching modules in neighboring networks the same color,\n",
    "- `\"nodes\"` colors every node by its module in one network, so you can see where each module goes,\n",
    "- `\"hierarchy\"` gives sub-modules colors close to their parent's (see the next section), and\n",
    "- `None` leaves everything gray.\n",
    "\n",
    "A module id is a number, not a name. Infomap numbers the modules by flow, largest first, so the numbers change\n",
    "when modules change size. Here the two teams at the top, labeled Cal and Ike, swap numbers between 2021 and 2022:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "3a8e9cc8",
   "metadata": {

     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-21T09:16:39.910853Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-21T09:16:40.244302Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-21T09:16:40.242168Z"
    }
   },

      "2022: Cal's team is module 3, Ike's team is module 4\n",
      "2023: Cal's team is module 3, Ike's team is module 4\n"
     ]

    "\n",

   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "9702fb4b",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "\n",
    "With `\"module_id\"`, the two teams swap colors in 2022, and their streamlines change color on the way. With\n",
    "`\"similarity\"`, each team keeps its color, because modules are matched by the nodes they share.\n",
    "\n",
    "`\"nodes\"` paints every node by its module in one network, the *color network*, and keeps that color in every\n",
    "network. `color_network=` picks it, as selecting a network does in the web app: an index, a network id, or a name\n",
    "given with `names=`. The default is the first network. Coloring by the first network shows where each module goes;\n",
    "coloring by the last shows where each module came from.\n",
    "\n",
    "`scheme=` picks one of the web app's color schemes (`alluvial.SCHEMES`), and `palette=` recolors at draw time with\n",
    "a list of colors or a matplotlib colormap, for example `palette=\"tab10\"`.\n"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "## Sub-modules\n",
    "\n",
    "Infomap finds a hierarchy of modules: here, departments with teams inside. `module_level=2` opens every module that\n",
    "has sub-modules (the same as clicking it in the web app). Pass one level per network to open only some of them, for\n",
    "example `module_level=[2, 1, 1]`. Gray boxes behind the sub-modules mark their parent module, as in the web app.\n",
    "`hierarchy=\"outline\"` draws a solid dark gray line around each parent instead, and `hierarchy=False` draws nothing.\n",
    "\n",
    "Sub-modules are colored like any other module. With the default `\"module_id\"`, a sub-module's color follows its\n",
    "path, such as `\"1:2\"`, so the same path has the same color in every network. `colors=\"hierarchy\"` gives sub-modules\n",
    "colors close to their parent's. `colors=\"similarity\"` pairs modules one at a time, as the web app does, and a\n",
    "module it cannot pair stays gray."
   ]
  },

    "## Highlighting groups of nodes\n",
    "\n",
    "`highlight=` colors chosen nodes wherever they go and leaves the rest gray. It takes `{label: node ids}`, and\n",
    "`legend=True` adds a legend. The label lines take the color of their node. Here we follow two teams."

    "teams = {\"Ada's team\": TEAMS[0], \"Max's team\": TEAMS[2]}  # node ids\n",

  {

   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "With `identifier=\"name\"`, nodes are matched by name, and `highlight` takes names too. `highlight` also accepts a\n",
    "function that gets an `alluvial.NodeInfo` (network, id, name, flow, module path, metadata) and returns a label or\n",
    "`None`. `alluvial.legend(ax, ...)` replaces the legend and takes the keywords of `Axes.legend`. `other=` adds an\n",
    "entry for the gray nodes."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",

   "id": "3e501e52",
   "metadata": {

   "source": [
    "def first_letter(node):\n",
    "    return \"A–F\" if node.name[0] <= \"F\" else None\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.2), layout=\"constrained\")\n",
    "alluvial.plot(\n",
    "    [im_a, im_b, im_c],\n",
    "    ax=ax,\n",
    "    names=YEARS,\n",
    "    identifier=\"name\",\n",
    "    highlight=first_letter,\n",
    "    highlight_colors=[\"tab:orange\"],\n",
    ")\n",
    "alluvial.legend(ax, other=\"others\", title=\"name starts with\", ncols=2);"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "d7a85b96",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## State networks: multilayer and memory\n",
    "\n",
    "The three years can also be one multilayer network, with one layer per year. A single Infomap run then finds\n",
    "modules that span the years. A multilayer network is a *state network*: each person has one state node per layer.\n",
    "`alluvial` reads the state nodes and labels them by their physical names. `split_layers=True` draws one network per\n",
    "layer and matches the layers by physical node, as the web app's \"split layers\" does."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 11,
   "id": "c40a3cc1",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-21T09:16:42.085756Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-21T09:16:42.085274Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-21T09:16:42.738703Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-21T09:16:42.736771Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "5 modules across 3 layers\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 800x300 with 2 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "ml = infomap.Infomap(seed=42, num_trials=10, silent=True)  # relax rate: Infomap's default, 0.15\n",
    "ml.set_names(dict(enumerate(NAMES)))\n",
    "for layer, year in enumerate(YEARS, start=1):\n",
    "    for u, v in links[year]:\n",
    "        ml.add_multilayer_intra_link(layer, u, v)\n",
    "ml.run()\n",
    "top_modules = {node.path.split(\":\")[0] for node in alluvial.read(ml).nodes}\n",
    "print(f\"{len(top_modules)} modules across {len(YEARS)} layers\")\n",
    "\n",
    "fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 3), layout=\"constrained\", width_ratios=[1, 2.2])\n",
    "alluvial.plot([ml], ax=axs[0], names=[\"all years\"])\n",
    "alluvial.plot([ml], ax=axs[1], split_layers=True, names=YEARS)\n",
    "axs[1].set_title(\"split_layers=True\", fontsize=\"medium\");"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "5ddf8155",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Memory (higher-order) networks work the same way. Their nodes are state nodes too.\n",
    "\n",
    "Matching state networks with each other needs care. With the default `identifier=\"id\"`, state nodes are matched by\n",
    "state id. That is right only if the state ids mean the same thing in every network. Use `identifier=\"name\"` to match\n",
    "by physical node name instead. Do not mix state networks and ordinary networks under `identifier=\"id\"`: a state id\n",
    "would be compared with a node id. `alluvial` warns when you do."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "dc48efa7",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Reading Infomap output files\n",
    "\n",
    "Infomap's output files work as inputs: `.tree`, `.ftree`, `.clu`, the state versions `.stree`/`*_states.tree`, and\n",
    "`-o json`. The format comes from the suffix. The default network name is the file name. Below we write the three\n",
    "runs from Python, which gives the same files as the command line `infomap net.net out/ -o tree,ftree,json`."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 12,
   "id": "d4cd925a",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-21T09:16:42.744867Z",

     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "from pathlib import Path\n",
    "\n",
    "out = Path(\"tutorial_output\")\n",
    "out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n",
    "for year, im in zip(YEARS, (im_a, im_b, im_c)):\n",

   "source": [
    "## Naming and ordering modules\n",
    "\n",
    "For a figure you usually want named modules in a fixed order. `module_names` replaces a module's node-name label\n",
    "by your own name, and `module_order` stacks modules bottom to top. Both refer to modules by network and module id.\n",
    "A network is its index (`0`, `1`, ...), its network id, or the name given with `names=` (as a string). A module id is a string,\n",
    "`\"3\"`, or `\"3:1\"` after `module_level=2` or `expand`. Get the ids from a plain `layout` first:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 14,
   "id": "878eee11",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-21T09:16:42.940576Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-21T09:16:42.939406Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-21T09:16:42.954687Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-21T09:16:42.952474Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "0 net0 2021 ['1', '2', '3', '4']\n",
      "1 net1 2022 ['1', '2', '3', '4']\n",
      "2 net2 2023 ['1', '2', '3', '4']\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "geometry = alluvial.layout([im_a, im_b, im_c], names=YEARS)\n",
    "for network in geometry.networks:\n",
    "    print(network.index, network.id, network.name, [module.id for module in network.modules])"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "71561516",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Module ids are per network: module `\"1\"` of 2021 and module `\"1\"` of 2022 are unrelated. To name the same\n",
    "group consistently across years, pass a callable. It gets a `ModuleInfo` for every module (`node_names`,\n",
    "`flow`, `id`, `network_index`, ...) and returns a name, or `None` to keep the node names. Here a module is named\n",
    "after the teams with at least four of their six members in it.\n",
    "\n",
    "`module_order={network: [module_id, ...]}` lists modules bottom to top. `...` stands for the modules you do not\n",
    "list, which keep their order, so `[m, ...]` puts module `m` at the bottom and `[..., m]` at the top. Below, the\n",
    "module with Ada is at the bottom in every year, and each network gets its own id from Infomap's partition."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 15,
   "id": "e17be4e7",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-21T09:16:42.959410Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-21T09:16:42.959065Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-21T09:16:43.287489Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-21T09:16:43.284689Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "{0: ['1', Ellipsis], 1: ['1', Ellipsis], 2: ['1', Ellipsis]}\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 600x300 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "LEADERS = {NAMES[team[0]]: team for team in TEAMS}  # each team by its first member\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "def team_name(module):\n",
    "    \"Name a module after the teams that have at least four of their members in it.\"\n",
    "    members = set(module.node_names)\n",
    "    teams = [leader for leader, team in LEADERS.items() if sum(NAMES[u] in members for u in team) >= 4]\n",
    "    return \" + \".join(teams) or None\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "def module_of(im, name):\n",
    "    \"The top module of the node with this name.\"\n",
    "    node = next(node for node in alluvial.read(im).nodes if node.name == name)\n",
    "    return node.path.split(\":\")[0]\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "ims = [im_a, im_b, im_c]\n",
    "ada_at_bottom = {i: [module_of(im, \"Ada\"), ...] for i, im in enumerate(ims)}\n",
    "print(ada_at_bottom)\n",
    "\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3), layout=\"constrained\")\n",
    "alluvial.plot(ims, ax=ax, names=YEARS, module_names=team_name, module_order=ada_at_bottom);"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "9d254171",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Some things to know:\n",
    "\n",
    "- Names are drawn as labels on the first and last network only, as in the web app. Names of middle networks\n",
    "  are kept (`ModuleGeometry.name`) but not drawn.\n",
    "- Only visible modules can be ordered. A module below `flow_threshold` raises an error.\n",
    "- `module_order` reorders all listed modules with one layout, so it stays fast with hundreds of sub-modules.\n",
    "  \"Move up/down\" in the web app gives the same order.\n",
    "- `save_diagram` stores the names and the custom order, and `layout` of the saved files restores them.\n",
    "\n",
    "Wrong ids raise an error that says what is wrong:"

   "source": [
    "## A figure for a paper\n",
    "\n",
    "Set your paper's font in `rcParams`; every font size in the diagram follows `font.size`. Pass your own axes, use\n",
    "`layout=\"constrained\"`, and save as PDF. Labels and limits are fitted again whenever the figure is drawn, so text\n",
    "keeps its point size and stays inside each panel. Long names are cut with an ellipsis, and a label that would\n",
    "collide with its neighbor loses lines."
   ]
  },

    "## Open in the web app\n",
    "\n",
    "`alluvial.save_diagram` takes the same arguments as `layout` and saves the diagram for the\n",
    "[web app](https://www.mapequation.org/alluvial), where you can fine-tune it by hand: move and name modules, recolor,\n",
    "change the layout. It writes the web app's \"Download diagram\" format, one Infomap JSON file per network in a `.zip` (or loose files\n",
    "with `loose=True`): drop the zip on the web app's load dialog. The files keep the networks, their names, the colors,\n",
    "the expanded modules, the layout options, the color scheme, module names and custom module orders.\n",
    "\n",
    "`alluvial.read` loads the `.zip` back as one network per file, and `layout`/`plot` restore the diagram from them.\n",
    "(The 2019 saved-diagram format, one `.json` with all networks, is no longer supported.)"
   ]

    "## Common mistakes\n",
    "\n",
    "`alluvial` raises or warns where a diagram would silently be wrong:\n",
    "\n",
    "- an Infomap object that has not run raises `ValueError: ... call im.run() first`,\n",
    "- a missing file raises `FileNotFoundError`,\n",
    "- `highlight` identifiers that match no node, and a `module_level` deeper than a network's module tree, give a\n",
    "  warning."
   ]
